questions.question: Which IPv4 subnet contains the host address 192.0.2.77/27?
questions.explanation: A /27 divides the final octet into blocks of 32. Octet 77 is in the interval 64–95.

option_explanations.C: A /27 divides the final octet into blocks of 32. Octet 77 is in the interval 64–95.

questions.question: What is the longest IPv4 prefix that provides at least 50 usable host addresses in a conventional LAN subnet?
questions.explanation: A /26 leaves six host bits. Its 64 addresses provide 62 usable host addresses after reserving network and broadcast. A /27 provides only 30.

option_explanations.A: A /25 has enough addresses but is a shorter, larger subnet than required.
option_explanations.B: A /26 leaves six host bits. Its 64 addresses provide 62 usable host addresses after reserving network and broadcast. A /27 provides only 30.
option_explanations.C: A /27 has only 30 ordinary usable hosts.
option_explanations.D: A /28 has only 14 ordinary usable hosts.
